text:
St. Louis played the better game and lost it in the last 69 seconds. Cole Smith scored a shorthanded goal at 18:51 of the third, the kind of chance that goes in two times out of three, and Frank Nazar added an empty-looking 87 percent finish at 19:56 after Connor McMichael had cut the lead to one on the power play. The Blues out-attempted Chicago 60 to 41 and held the edge at even strength, 2.12 expected goals to 1.07. Replay every shot and St. Louis wins 74 percent of the time.

Mason McTavish gave the Blues a 1-0 lead late in the first, and the game turned in the second. Sam Rinzel tied it on a power play at 5:40, and Anton Frondell put Chicago ahead two minutes later on a snap shot. That period was Chicago's best (1.04 expected goals to 0.57), but it produced only two chances of note, and the Blackhawks needed both. The third was a trade of chances, 2.06 for St. Louis and 1.81 for Chicago, with the Blues pressing for the tying goal while the game stayed open.

Spencer Knight earned the first star by stopping 25 of 27 and saving about 1.2 goals more than the chances he faced would suggest. Joel Hofer was roughly average on 19 shots. Nazar finished with a goal and an assist on 1.05 individual expected goals, and Frondell added a goal and an assist. Chicago scored four times on 3.35 expected goals, which is fair enough, but St. Louis created nearly as much and lost anyway, mostly because of one late minute and a goalie who made the difference.
